name: Andhra Pradesh
tagline: Hill coffee, a red-rock canyon and the temples of Tirumala
intro: Andhra Pradesh runs from the Eastern Ghats coffee country above Visakhapatnam to the pilgrim hills of Tirumala and the Deccan rock country around Gandikota. It rewards travellers who mix beaches, cave systems and Vijayanagara-era temples with some of the best Andhra cooking you will find. Most of the state is an easy drive or short flight from Hyderabad.
photoAlt: The Pennar River winding through the red sandstone gorge at Gandikota

destinations.name: Visakhapatnam
destinations.blurb: A port city with long beaches, the INS Kursura submarine museum and Kailasagiri hill views over the Bay of Bengal.

destinations.name: Araku Valley
destinations.blurb: Coffee estates, tribal villages and cool air in the Eastern Ghats, reached by a scenic rail line through dozens of tunnels.

destinations.name: Gandikota
destinations.blurb: A 13th-century fort perched above a deep red canyon cut by the Pennar River, best seen at sunrise.

destinations.name: Belum Caves
destinations.blurb: The second-longest cave system on the Indian subcontinent, with lit passages, stalactites and underground chambers.

destinations.name: Amaravati
destinations.blurb: The ancient Buddhist stupa site on the Krishna, with a museum of finely carved limestone panels.

destinations.name: Borra Caves
destinations.blurb: Million-year-old limestone caves in the Ananthagiri hills, with stalactites lit up along the walkways and the Araku railway passing overhead.

destinations.name: Papikondalu
destinations.blurb: A launch cruise through the Godavari gorge, where the river narrows between steep forested hills of the Eastern Ghats.

devotional.name: Sri Venkateswara Temple, Tirumala
devotional.blurb: The hilltop shrine to Lord Venkateswara draws tens of thousands of pilgrims a day, many climbing the stone steps from Tirupati and offering their hair.

devotional.name: Srisailam
devotional.blurb: The Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga and Bhramaramba Shakti Peetha share one walled temple above the Krishna gorge in the Nallamala forest.

devotional.name: Lepakshi Veerabhadra Temple
devotional.blurb: A 16th-century Vijayanagara temple to Veerabhadra, known for its painted ceilings, a pillar that does not touch the floor and a huge monolithic Nandi.

devotional.name: Srikalahasti Temple
devotional.blurb: A Shiva temple on the Swarnamukhi river revered as the Vayu (wind) linga, where many devotees perform Rahu–Ketu puja.

devotional.name: Simhachalam
devotional.blurb: A hilltop temple outside Visakhapatnam to Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha, whose idol stays covered in sandalwood paste except on one day a year.

devotional.name: Kanaka Durga Temple, Vijayawada
devotional.blurb: The goddess Durga is worshipped on Indrakeeladri hill above the Krishna, with the city filling up for the Dasara festival.

devotional.name: Gunadala Mary Matha Shrine
devotional.blurb: A Catholic hillside shrine in Vijayawada whose February feast draws lakhs of pilgrims of every faith.

devotional.name: Ameen Peer Dargah, Kadapa
devotional.blurb: A 17th-century Sufi shrine visited by Muslims and Hindus alike, especially during its annual urs.

highlights: Ride the Visakhapatnam–Araku train through the Eastern Ghats
Walk through Borra Caves' limestone formations
Watch sunrise over the Gandikota canyon
Darshan at Tirumala's Sri Venkateswara Temple
See the painted ceilings and hanging pillar at Lepakshi
Taste Araku coffee and bamboo chicken in the hills

days.title: Arrive Visakhapatnam
days.details: Arrive in Vizag and spend the afternoon at RK Beach and the submarine museum. End with sunset views from Kailasagiri hill.

days.title: Vizag to Araku via Borra Caves
days.details: Drive about 3 hours into the Eastern Ghats, stopping at Borra Caves and the Ananthagiri coffee viewpoints. Overnight in Araku.

days.title: Araku Valley
days.details: Visit the Tribal Museum, the coffee museum and Padmapuram Gardens, with a stop at the Galikonda viewpoint. Return by the afternoon train to Vizag for the tunnel-and-bridge views.

days.title: Simhachalam and departure
days.details: Morning visit to the hilltop Simhachalam temple, then transfer to Visakhapatnam airport.

itineraries.title: Temples, Caves and Canyons of Rayalaseema

days.title: Arrive Tirupati
days.details: Arrive at Tirupati airport or station and settle in. Evening visit to the Sri Govindaraja Swamy Temple in town.

days.title: Tirumala
days.details: Drive up the ghat road to Tirumala for darshan at the Sri Venkateswara Temple, with time for Silathoranam and Akasa Ganga.

days.title: Srikalahasti to Gandikota
days.details: Visit the Srikalahasti temple (40 minutes from Tirupati), then drive about 5 hours to Gandikota. Overnight near the fort.

days.title: Gandikota and Belum Caves
days.details: Sunrise at the canyon rim and a walk through the fort, then drive about 1.5 hours to explore Belum Caves. Return to Gandikota for the night.

days.title: Gandikota to Lepakshi
days.details: Drive about 4 hours south to Lepakshi through the dry Rayalaseema plateau. Afternoon at the Veerabhadra Temple and the great Nandi.

days.title: Puttaparthi and Penukonda
days.details: Day trip to Penukonda fort and the Puttaparthi ashram town, each under 1.5 hours from Lepakshi. Return for the night.

days.title: Departure
days.details: Transfer to Bengaluru airport, about 1.5–2 hours from Lepakshi, for onward flights.

name: Arunachal Pradesh
tagline: High passes, Monpa monasteries and the rice terraces of Ziro
intro: Arunachal Pradesh climbs from the Brahmaputra plains to Himalayan passes above 4,000 metres, with dozens of tribal communities along the way. The road to Tawang crosses Sela Pass to reach one of the largest Buddhist monasteries in India, while Ziro's Apatani villages sit in a broad valley of paddy and pine. Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit and foreigners a Protected Area Permit, which we arrange.
photoAlt: Tawang Monastery spread across a ridge above the Tawang valley with mountains behind

destinations.name: Tawang
destinations.blurb: A high valley town near the Bum La border pass, with a war memorial, cold lakes and the snow road over Sela on the way in.

destinations.name: Ziro
destinations.blurb: A green valley of Apatani villages and paddy fields, host to the Ziro Festival of Music each September.

destinations.name: Dirang
destinations.blurb: A riverside stop with a stone dzong village, hot springs and apple and kiwi orchards.

destinations.name: Bomdila
destinations.blurb: A hill town with craft centres, apple orchards and wide views of the eastern Himalaya on the way to Tawang.

destinations.name: Sela Pass
destinations.blurb: A 4,170-metre pass with a frozen lake for much of the winter, now bypassed by the Sela Tunnel.

destinations.name: Namdapha National Park
destinations.blurb: A vast rainforest reserve in the far east, home to hoolock gibbons and all four big cats of the region.

destinations.name: Itanagar
destinations.blurb: The capital, with the brick ruins of Ita Fort and a good state museum on tribal cultures.

devotional.name: Tawang Monastery
devotional.blurb: Founded in 1680–81, it is the largest Buddhist monastery in India, home to several hundred Gelugpa monks and a gilded eight-metre Buddha.

devotional.name: Urgelling Monastery
devotional.blurb: A small gompa just below Tawang town, venerated as the birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama, Tsangyang Gyatso.

devotional.name: Bomdila Monastery
devotional.blurb: Gentse Gaden Rabgye Ling, a Gelugpa monastery above Bomdila built in 1965 as a replica of the Tsona Gontse monastery in Tibet.

devotional.name: Golden Pagoda, Namsai
devotional.blurb: A gilded Theravada Buddhist pagoda of the Tai Khamti community, set among gardens and ponds in eastern Arunachal.

devotional.name: Parshuram Kund
devotional.blurb: A sacred pool on the Lohit river where thousands of Hindu pilgrims bathe at Makar Sankranti each January.

devotional.name: Malinithan
devotional.blurb: Hilltop ruins of a granite temple to the goddess Durga near Likabali, linked by legend to Krishna and Rukmini, with a shrine still in worship.

highlights: Cross Sela Pass and stop at its high-altitude lake
Join morning prayers at Tawang Monastery
Drive to Bum La and Sangetsar (Madhuri) Lake with permits
Walk through Apatani villages in the Ziro valley
Visit the Tawang War Memorial
Soak in the hot springs at Dirang

days.title: Arrive Itanagar
days.details: Arrive at Donyi Polo Airport and transfer to Itanagar. Visit Ita Fort and the Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum.

days.title: Itanagar to Ziro
days.details: Drive about 4 hours through forested hills to the Ziro valley. Evening walk along the paddy fields.

days.title: Apatani villages
days.details: Spend the day in Hong and Hija villages, meeting families and learning about their rice-and-fish farming. Visit the Siddheshwar Nath temple.

days.title: Pine forests and Talley Valley
days.details: Walk the pine and bamboo trails around Ziro, with an optional half-day trip toward Talley Valley Wildlife Sanctuary.

days.title: Return and depart
days.details: Drive back to Donyi Polo Airport, about 4 hours, for your onward flight.

itineraries.title: Tawang and the Western Arunachal Circuit

days.title: Guwahati to Bhalukpong
days.details: Leave Guwahati after arrival and drive about 5 hours to Bhalukpong on the Kameng River at the Arunachal border.

days.title: Bhalukpong to Dirang
days.details: Climb through Tenga and Bomdila to Dirang, about 6 hours with stops. Evening at the old dzong village.

days.title: Dirang to Tawang
days.details: Cross Sela Pass or the Sela Tunnel and stop at the Jaswant Garh memorial on the 5-hour drive. Overnight in Tawang.

days.title: Tawang sightseeing
days.details: Visit Tawang Monastery, the Urgelling birthplace of the sixth Dalai Lama and the Tawang War Memorial at sunset.

days.title: Bum La and Sangetsar Lake
days.details: Full-day excursion by local vehicle to the Bum La pass and Sangetsar Lake, subject to army permits and weather.

days.title: Tawang to Bomdila
days.details: Drive back over Sela, about 6 hours, to Bomdila. Visit the Gontse Gaden Rabgyel Lling monastery.

days.title: Bomdila to Guwahati
days.details: A long scenic drive of about 7–8 hours down to the plains and Guwahati.

days.title: Departure
days.details: Transfer to Guwahati airport, with a morning visit to Kamakhya Temple if time allows.

name: Assam
tagline: One-horned rhinos, river islands and tea by the Brahmaputra
intro: Assam follows the Brahmaputra through grasslands, tea estates and the old Ahom kingdom's capitals. Kaziranga offers some of the best rhino and wild elephant sightings in Asia, while Majuli's satras keep alive a centuries-old Vaishnav tradition of dance and mask-making. Guwahati is the gateway, with good air connections from across India.
photoAlt: Tall grassland and wetlands of Kaziranga National Park with wildlife grazing

destinations.name: Kaziranga National Park
destinations.blurb: A UNESCO site holding about two-thirds of the world's one-horned rhinos, explored by jeep safari.

destinations.name: Majuli
destinations.blurb: A large river island in the Brahmaputra with mask-makers, potters, Mising stilt villages and slow cycling between paddy fields.

destinations.name: Guwahati
destinations.blurb: The gateway city on the Brahmaputra, with sunset river cruises, the Assam State Museum and busy Fancy Bazaar.

destinations.name: Sivasagar
destinations.blurb: The former Ahom capital with the Rang Ghar royal pavilion, the Talatal Ghar palace and the Kareng Ghar.

destinations.name: Manas National Park
destinations.blurb: A forest and grassland reserve on the Bhutan border, home to tigers, golden langurs and wild buffalo.

destinations.name: Dibrugarh
destinations.blurb: Tea country in Upper Assam, with heritage planter bungalows set inside working estates.

destinations.name: Jorhat
destinations.blurb: A tea town and the jumping-off point for the ferry to Majuli, with the Tocklai tea research centre.

devotional.name: Kamakhya Temple
devotional.blurb: A Shakti Peetha on Nilachal hill above Guwahati, central to Tantric worship and crowded with pilgrims during the Ambubachi Mela each June.

devotional.name: Umananda Temple
devotional.blurb: A Shiva temple on Peacock Island in the middle of the Brahmaputra, reached by a short ferry from Guwahati.

devotional.name: Hajo
devotional.blurb: A town shared by faiths: the Hayagriva Madhava temple is sacred to Hindus and Buddhists, while the Poa Mecca mosque is said to hold a quarter of Mecca's sanctity.

devotional.name: Barpeta Satra
devotional.blurb: A Vaishnav monastery founded in the 16th century by Madhavdeva, known for its namghar prayer hall and Holi celebrations.

devotional.name: Auniati Satra, Majuli
devotional.blurb: One of the oldest satras on Majuli, where monks keep alive Sankardeva's devotional music, dance and a small museum of Ahom-era artefacts.

devotional.name: Sivadol, Sivasagar
devotional.blurb: An 18th-century Ahom temple to Shiva on the bank of the Sivasagar tank, its gold-topped tower among the tallest Hindu temples in India.

devotional.name: Gurdwara Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib, Dhubri
devotional.blurb: A gurdwara on the Brahmaputra marking the visit of Guru Nanak and, later, Guru Tegh Bahadur, with a large gathering each winter.

highlights: Early-morning jeep safari in Kaziranga's central range
Ferry across the Brahmaputra to Majuli
Watch a satriya dance performance at a Majuli satra
Stay in a heritage tea bungalow near Dibrugarh
Sunset cruise on the Brahmaputra at Guwahati
Explore Ahom monuments at Sivasagar

days.title: Arrive Guwahati
days.details: Visit Kamakhya Temple on Nilachal Hill and take an evening cruise on the Brahmaputra.

days.title: Guwahati to Kaziranga
days.details: Drive about 5 hours east along the highway to Kaziranga. Evening walk through a nearby tea garden.

days.title: Kaziranga safaris
days.details: Morning jeep safari in the Central (Kohora) range and an afternoon safari in the Western (Bagori) range for rhinos, elephants and swamp deer.

days.title: Return and depart
days.details: Drive back to Guwahati airport, about 5 hours, for your onward flight.

itineraries.title: Assam from Rhinos to River Islands

days.title: Arrive Guwahati
days.details: Visit Kamakhya Temple and the Assam State Museum, then an evening Brahmaputra cruise.

days.title: Guwahati to Kaziranga
days.details: Drive about 5 hours to Kaziranga, stopping at a roadside dhaba for an Assamese thali.

days.title: Kaziranga
days.details: Morning and afternoon jeep safaris in different ranges, with a visit to the Kaziranga Orchid Park in between.

days.title: Kaziranga to Majuli
days.details: Drive about 2.5 hours to Nimati Ghat near Jorhat and take the ferry across to Majuli. Overnight in a bamboo cottage.

days.title: Majuli satras
days.details: Visit the Kamalabari and Auniati satras and the mask-makers of Samaguri, then cycle through Mising villages.

days.title: Majuli to Sivasagar
days.details: Ferry back to Jorhat and drive about 1.5 hours to Sivasagar for the Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar and Shivadol. Continue 2 hours to Dibrugarh.

days.title: Dibrugarh tea country
days.details: Tour a working tea estate and factory, with a tasting and a relaxed afternoon at your planter's bungalow.

days.title: Departure
days.details: Transfer to Dibrugarh airport for your flight home.

name: Bihar
tagline: Where the Buddha found enlightenment and Nalanda taught Asia
intro: Bihar holds the heart of the Buddhist world: Bodh Gaya, where the Buddha attained enlightenment, the hills of Rajgir where he preached, and the ruins of Nalanda's great monastic university. It is also sacred to Jains, with Pawapuri and Vaishali close by. Distances are short, so the main sites fit easily into a week.
photoAlt: The tall brick spire of the Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya surrounded by stupas

destinations.name: Nalanda
destinations.blurb: Excavated ruins of a monastic university that drew scholars from across Asia between the 5th and 12th centuries.

destinations.name: Rajgir
destinations.blurb: A ring of hills with Vulture's Peak, a ropeway up Ratnagiri, the cyclopean wall and natural hot springs.

destinations.name: Patna
destinations.blurb: The state capital on the Ganga, with the Bihar Museum, the Golghar granary and Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Library.

destinations.name: Vaishali
destinations.blurb: An ancient republic with an Ashokan lion pillar and the birthplace of Mahavira nearby.

destinations.name: Kesariya
destinations.blurb: Home to one of the tallest excavated Buddhist stupas in the world, rising in terraced brick levels.

destinations.name: Vikramshila
destinations.blurb: Excavated ruins near Bhagalpur of a Pala-era monastic university, with a large cruciform stupa at its centre.

destinations.name: Valmiki Tiger Reserve
destinations.blurb: Sal forest and grassland on the Nepal border in West Champaran, with tigers, gaur and river safaris on the Gandak.

devotional.name: Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya
devotional.blurb: Buddhists from across the world come to meditate under the Bodhi Tree where the Buddha attained enlightenment, beside the brick temple tower.

devotional.name: Vishnupad Temple, Gaya
devotional.blurb: A temple built around a footprint of Vishnu in basalt, where Hindus perform pind daan rites for their ancestors, especially during Pitru Paksha.

devotional.name: Takht Sri Patna Sahib
devotional.blurb: One of the five takhts of Sikhism, built at the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh in old Patna.

devotional.name: Vishwa Shanti Stupa, Rajgir
devotional.blurb: A white peace pagoda on Ratnagiri hill reached by chairlift, with gold statues marking the four stages of the Buddha's life.

devotional.name: Pawapuri Jal Mandir
devotional.blurb: A white marble Jain temple in a lotus pond marking the place where Mahavira attained nirvana, lit with lamps at Diwali.

devotional.name: Maner Sharif
devotional.blurb: The dargah of the Sufi saint Makhdoom Yahya Maneri and the Mughal-era tomb of Shah Daulat, west of Patna.

devotional.name: Mundeshwari Temple
devotional.blurb: An octagonal stone temple in Kaimur district, dated to around the 6th century and considered one of the oldest Hindu temples still in worship.

highlights: Evening meditation under the Bodhi Tree at the Mahabodhi Temple
Walk the brick monasteries and temples of ancient Nalanda
Climb to Vulture's Peak in Rajgir at sunrise
See the Didarganj Yakshi at the Bihar Museum in Patna
Visit the Jal Mandir at Pawapuri
Tour the international monasteries of Bodh Gaya

days.title: Arrive Patna
days.details: Spend the afternoon at the Bihar Museum and Golghar, with an evening by the Ganga ghats.

days.title: Patna to Nalanda and Rajgir
days.details: Drive about 2.5 hours to Nalanda to explore the university ruins and museum, then continue 30 minutes to Rajgir.

days.title: Rajgir to Bodh Gaya
days.details: Take the ropeway to the Vishwa Shanti Stupa and walk up to Vulture's Peak, then drive about 2 hours to Bodh Gaya.

days.title: Bodh Gaya and departure
days.details: Morning at the Mahabodhi Temple and the Great Buddha Statue, then transfer to Gaya airport, 20 minutes away.

days.title: Arrive Patna
days.details: Visit the Bihar Museum, Golghar and Takht Sri Patna Sahib gurdwara.

days.title: Vaishali and Kesariya
days.details: Cross the Ganga to Vaishali, about 1.5 hours, for the Ashokan pillar and relic stupa, then drive 2 hours to the Kesariya stupa. Return to Patna in the evening.

days.title: Patna to Nalanda
days.details: Drive about 2.5 hours to Nalanda for the ruins, the museum and the Xuanzang Memorial Hall. Overnight in Rajgir.

days.title: Rajgir
days.details: Visit Vulture's Peak, the Vishwa Shanti Stupa, the hot springs and the Rajgir Nature Safari.

days.title: Pawapuri to Bodh Gaya
days.details: Stop at the Jal Mandir in Pawapuri, 40 minutes from Rajgir, then continue about 2.5 hours to Bodh Gaya.

days.title: Bodh Gaya
days.details: A full day at the Mahabodhi Temple, the Thai, Japanese and Bhutanese monasteries, and the Dungeshwari caves across the Phalgu river.

days.title: Departure
days.details: Transfer to Gaya airport or station for onward travel.

name: Chhattisgarh
tagline: Bastar waterfalls, limestone caves and tribal market days
intro: Chhattisgarh is forest country, best known for the Bastar region around Jagdalpur, where the Indravati River drops over the wide Chitrakote Falls. Weekly tribal haats, dhokra metalwork and the caves of Kanger Valley make it one of central India's most distinctive trips. Raipur and Jagdalpur airports make Bastar easier to reach than most people expect.
photoAlt: The broad horseshoe of Chitrakote Falls on the Indravati River in Bastar

destinations.name: Chitrakote Falls
destinations.blurb: A horseshoe-shaped waterfall nearly 300 metres wide on the Indravati, at its fullest after the monsoon.

destinations.name: Kanger Valley National Park
destinations.blurb: Sal forest with the Kotumsar and Kailash limestone caves and the stepped Tirathgarh Falls.

destinations.name: Jagdalpur
destinations.blurb: The Bastar capital, with an old palace, the Anthropological Museum and access to the region's haats.

destinations.name: Sirpur
destinations.blurb: A riverside archaeological site with excavated Buddhist monasteries and the 7th-century brick Lakshmana Temple.

destinations.name: Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary
destinations.blurb: A compact reserve near Raipur known for leopards, gaur and good birding.

destinations.name: Kondagaon
destinations.blurb: A crafts town where artisans cast dhokra bell-metal figures by the lost-wax method.

destinations.name: Mainpat
destinations.blurb: A cool plateau in Surguja with a Tibetan settlement, waterfalls and the odd bouncing "Ulta Pani" ground.

devotional.name: Danteshwari Temple, Dantewada
devotional.blurb: The shrine of Bastar's presiding goddess at the meeting of the Shankini and Dankini rivers, central to the 75-day Bastar Dussehra.

devotional.name: Bhoramdeo Temple
devotional.blurb: An 11th-century stone temple to Shiva in the Maikal hills, its carved walls often compared to Khajuraho.

devotional.name: Mahamaya Temple, Ratanpur
devotional.blurb: An old Kalachuri-era shrine to the goddess Mahamaya near Bilaspur, crowded during the two Navratris.

devotional.name: Bambleshwari Temple, Dongargarh
devotional.blurb: A hilltop temple to the goddess Bamleshwari reached by about a thousand steps or a ropeway.

devotional.name: Rajim
devotional.blurb: The Rajiv Lochan Temple stands at the confluence of the Mahanadi, Pairi and Sondur, where the Rajim Kumbh fair is held each February.

devotional.name: Giraudpuri Dham
devotional.blurb: The birthplace of Guru Ghasidas, founder of the Satnami sect, marked by the 77-metre Jaitkham tower.

highlights: Boat ride to the foot of Chitrakote Falls
Walk into the Kotumsar limestone cave
Browse a weekly tribal haat in Bastar
Watch dhokra casting at Kondagaon
See the brick Lakshmana Temple at Sirpur
Experience Bastar Dussehra if travelling in October

days.title: Arrive Jagdalpur
days.details: Fly into Jagdalpur and visit the Anthropological Museum and the Danteshwari shrine in the old palace.

days.title: Chitrakote Falls
days.details: Drive about 1 hour to Chitrakote for the falls by day and a boat ride near the base, staying for the sunset light.

days.title: Kanger Valley
days.details: Explore Tirathgarh Falls and the Kotumsar cave in Kanger Valley National Park, about 1 hour from Jagdalpur. Cave access depends on season.

days.title: Haat and departure
days.details: Visit a nearby weekly market if the day lines up, then fly out of Jagdalpur.

days.title: Arrive Raipur
days.details: Arrive in Raipur and visit the Mahant Ghasidas Museum and the Purkhauti Muktangan open-air museum.

days.title: Sirpur and Barnawapara
days.details: Drive about 1.5 hours to Sirpur's temples and monasteries, then continue to Barnawapara for an evening safari.

days.title: Raipur to Jagdalpur via Kondagaon
days.details: A full-day drive of about 6–7 hours south, stopping at Kondagaon to watch dhokra artisans at work.

days.title: Chitrakote Falls
days.details: Spend the day at Chitrakote, with a boat ride and a walk along the gorge. Overnight at Chitrakote.

days.title: Kanger Valley
days.details: Visit Tirathgarh Falls and the Kotumsar cave, then return to Jagdalpur.

days.title: Dantewada and Barsur
days.details: Drive about 2 hours to the Danteshwari Temple in Dantewada and the old temples of Barsur, returning to Jagdalpur.

days.title: Departure
days.details: Fly out of Jagdalpur, or drive back to Raipur for wider connections.

name: Goa
tagline: Baroque churches, laterite forts and slow afternoons by the sea
intro: Goa is far more than beach shacks: its Portuguese-era churches in Old Goa are a UNESCO site, Panaji's Fontainhas quarter is a pocket of painted Latin houses, and the Western Ghats hinterland hides spice farms and Dudhsagar Falls. North Goa is lively and social, while the south has quieter coves around Palolem and Agonda. It is a short flight from most Indian cities.
photoAlt: Dudhsagar Falls pouring down a forested cliff with a railway bridge crossing its face

destinations.name: Panaji and Fontainhas
destinations.blurb: The riverside capital, with a Latin quarter of colourful houses, tavernas and small galleries.

destinations.name: Palolem
destinations.blurb: A crescent beach in South Goa with calm water, kayaking and boat trips to spot dolphins.

destinations.name: Anjuna and Vagator
destinations.blurb: Red cliffs, the Wednesday flea market and sunsets from the ramparts of Chapora Fort.

destinations.name: Dudhsagar Falls
destinations.blurb: A four-tiered waterfall on the Mandovi in Bhagwan Mahavir Sanctuary, at its best just after the monsoon.

destinations.name: Divar Island
destinations.blurb: A short free ferry ride from Old Goa to quiet villages, paddy fields and old Goan homes.

destinations.name: Fort Aguada
destinations.blurb: A 17th-century Portuguese fort and lighthouse at the mouth of the Mandovi.

destinations.name: Cabo de Rama
destinations.blurb: A clifftop fort in South Goa with a small chapel and wide views over the Arabian Sea.

devotional.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
devotional.blurb: A 16th-century Jesuit church in Old Goa holding the remains of St Francis Xavier, displayed to pilgrims roughly once a decade.

devotional.name: Se Cathedral
devotional.blurb: The largest church in Old Goa, dedicated to St Catherine, with a gilded main altar and the Golden Bell in its tower.

devotional.name: Church of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception
devotional.blurb: The white zigzag staircase of this Panaji church leads to a bell brought from Old Goa, with a big feast each December.

devotional.name: Shri Mangueshi Temple
devotional.blurb: A hilltop temple to Shiva as Mangesh in Priol, Ponda, with a seven-storey lamp tower and a pale-yellow facade.

devotional.name: Shri Shantadurga Temple
devotional.blurb: A temple to the goddess Shantadurga at Kavlem, with Indo-Portuguese domes and an annual chariot festival.

devotional.name: Safa Masjid
devotional.blurb: A 1560 mosque in Ponda built by the Bijapur sultanate, with a stepped tank where worshippers wash before prayer.

devotional.name: Tambdi Surla Mahadev Temple
devotional.blurb: A small 12th-century Kadamba temple of black basalt in the forest, the oldest surviving temple in Goa.

highlights: Walk the churches of Old Goa
Heritage walk through Fontainhas with a stop for bebinca
Spice plantation lunch near Ponda
Jeep trip to Dudhsagar Falls
Sunset from Chapora Fort
Ferry ride to Divar Island

days.title: Arrive Goa
days.details: Arrive at Dabolim or Mopa airport and check in near Panaji. Evening walk through Fontainhas and dinner at a Goan restaurant.

days.title: Old Goa and Divar
days.details: Visit the Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral, then take the ferry to Divar Island for a village cycle ride.

days.title: North Goa coast
days.details: Fort Aguada in the morning, beach time at Candolim, and sunset from Chapora Fort above Vagator.

days.title: Spice farm and departure
days.details: Lunch at a spice plantation near Ponda, about 45 minutes from Panaji, before your flight out.

days.title: Arrive North Goa
days.details: Check in near Calangute or Anjuna and spend the afternoon on the beach.

days.title: Panaji and Old Goa
days.details: Fontainhas heritage walk in the morning and the churches of Old Goa in the afternoon, finishing with a Mandovi river cruise.

days.title: Forts and markets
days.details: Visit Fort Aguada and Chapora Fort, with the Anjuna flea market on Wednesdays or the Arpora night market on Saturdays.

days.title: Dudhsagar and spice farm
days.details: Drive about 1.5 hours to Collem for a jeep ride to Dudhsagar Falls, then lunch at a Ponda spice farm. Continue south to Palolem.

days.title: Palolem and Butterfly Beach
days.details: Morning boat trip for dolphins and Butterfly Beach, with a slow afternoon in Palolem.

days.title: Cabo de Rama and Agonda
days.details: Visit the clifftop Cabo de Rama fort and spend the afternoon on quiet Agonda beach.

days.title: Departure
days.details: Transfer to Dabolim airport, about 1.5 hours from Palolem.

name: Gujarat
tagline: Salt desert nights, Asiatic lions and carved stepwells
intro: Gujarat packs a lot into one state: the white salt flats of the Great Rann of Kutch, the last wild Asiatic lions in Gir, and the stepwells and sun temples of the Solanki era. Ahmedabad's old city is a UNESCO World Heritage City, and the coast holds the pilgrim towns of Dwarka and Somnath. Kutch's craft villages make it a rewarding trip for textile lovers.
photoAlt: The carved stone galleries of Rani ki vav stepwell descending in tiers at Patan

destinations.name: Ahmedabad
destinations.blurb: A walled city of pols, carved havelis and mosques, plus the Sabarmati Ashram on the riverfront.

destinations.name: Great Rann of Kutch
destinations.blurb: A vast white salt desert near Dhordo, at its most striking under a full moon during the Rann Utsav season.

destinations.name: Bhuj
destinations.blurb: The Kutch capital, with the Aina Mahal and Prag Mahal and craft villages for block printing and embroidery nearby.

destinations.name: Gir National Park
destinations.blurb: The only wild home of the Asiatic lion, explored on jeep safaris from Sasan Gir.

destinations.name: Patan and Modhera
destinations.blurb: The Rani ki vav stepwell and the Modhera Sun Temple, two masterpieces of 11th-century Solanki architecture.

destinations.name: Statue of Unity
destinations.blurb: The world's tallest statue, overlooking the Narmada and the Sardar Sarovar Dam at Kevadia.

destinations.name: Champaner
destinations.blurb: A UNESCO-listed abandoned sultanate city at the foot of Pavagadh hill, with stone gateways, palace ruins and carved mosques.

destinations.name: Little Rann of Kutch
destinations.blurb: Flat salt pans near Dasada where the Indian wild ass roams, along with flamingos and cranes in winter.

devotional.name: Somnath Temple
devotional.blurb: The first of the twelve Jyotirlingas, rebuilt many times on the shore of the Arabian Sea, with an evening aarti and sound-and-light show.

devotional.name: Dwarkadhish Temple
devotional.blurb: A five-storey temple to Krishna at the mouth of the Gomti in Dwarka, its flag changed several times a day, with Bet Dwarka a boat ride away.

devotional.name: Palitana
devotional.blurb: More than 800 Jain temples crown Shatrunjaya hill, reached by about 3,500 steps climbed before the midday heat.

devotional.name: Girnar
devotional.blurb: A sacred mountain near Junagadh with Jain temples and Hindu shrines, including Ambaji at the top, climbed by nearly 10,000 steps or a ropeway.

devotional.name: Ambaji Temple
devotional.blurb: A major Shakti Peetha in the Aravalli hills where the goddess is worshipped as a sacred yantra rather than an idol, busiest at Bhadarvi Poonam.

devotional.name: Sidi Saiyyed Mosque
devotional.blurb: A 1573 mosque in Ahmedabad whose carved stone jali of an intertwining tree has become a symbol of the city.

devotional.name: Udvada Atash Behram
devotional.blurb: The oldest Zoroastrian fire temple in India, where a sacred fire has burned for more than 1,200 years in a small seaside village.

devotional.name: Akshardham, Gandhinagar
devotional.blurb: A pink sandstone Swaminarayan temple with carved pillars, gardens and an evening water show.

highlights: Full-moon evening on the white Rann at Dhordo
Lion safari in Gir National Park
Ahmedabad heritage walk through the old city pols
See Rani ki vav and the Modhera Sun Temple
Wild ass safari in the Little Rann of Kutch
Meet block printers and embroiderers in Kutch villages

itineraries.title: Ahmedabad, Stepwells and the Statue of Unity

days.title: Arrive Ahmedabad
days.details: Visit Sabarmati Ashram and the Sidi Saiyyed Mosque, with dinner at the Manek Chowk night market.

days.title: Modhera and Patan
days.details: Morning old-city heritage walk, then drive about 2 hours to the Modhera Sun Temple and 40 minutes on to Rani ki vav. Return to Ahmedabad.

days.title: Ahmedabad to Kevadia
days.details: Drive about 4 hours to the Statue of Unity for the viewing gallery, the Valley of Flowers and the evening laser show.

days.title: Departure
days.details: Transfer to Vadodara airport, about 2 hours away, for your flight.

days.title: Arrive Ahmedabad
days.details: Settle in and visit Sabarmati Ashram, then dinner at Manek Chowk.

days.title: Ahmedabad heritage
days.details: Morning heritage walk through the pols, the Calico Museum (by booking) and the Adalaj stepwell.

days.title: Modhera, Patan and the Little Rann
days.details: See the Modhera Sun Temple and Rani ki vav, then drive about 2 hours to Dasada on the edge of the Little Rann.

days.title: Little Rann to Bhuj
days.details: Early wild ass safari on the salt flats, then drive about 5 hours to Bhuj.

days.title: Kutch villages and the White Rann
days.details: Visit the craft villages of Bhujodi and Hodka, then drive to Dhordo for sunset on the White Rann.

days.title: Bhuj to Dwarka
days.details: Morning at the Aina Mahal and Prag Mahal, then a long drive of about 7 hours via Jamnagar to Dwarka.

days.title: Dwarka to Somnath
days.details: Morning darshan at Dwarkadhish Temple, then drive about 5 hours down the coast to Somnath for the evening aarti and light show.

days.title: Somnath to Gir
days.details: Drive about 1.5 hours to Sasan Gir for an afternoon jeep safari in search of lions.

days.title: Gir and departure
days.details: Morning safari, then transfer to Rajkot airport, about 3.5 hours away.

name: Haryana
tagline: Epic battlefields, Mughal gardens and winter birds near Delhi
intro: Haryana wraps around Delhi on three sides, so its sights make easy short trips from the capital. Kurukshetra is linked with the Bhagavad Gita and the Mahabharata, Pinjore's terraced gardens sit at the foot of the Shivaliks, and Sultanpur fills with migratory birds each winter. It is a good add-on to a Delhi or Chandigarh visit.
photoAlt: The wide water tank of Brahma Sarovar at Kurukshetra with temples along its edge

destinations.name: Sultanpur National Park
destinations.blurb: A wetland near Gurugram that draws flamingos, pelicans and cranes between October and March.

destinations.name: Pinjore Gardens
destinations.blurb: The terraced Mughal-style Yadavindra Gardens with fountains and pavilions near Chandigarh.

destinations.name: Morni Hills
destinations.blurb: The only hill station in Haryana, with twin lakes and pine forest walks in the Shivaliks.

destinations.name: Panipat
destinations.blurb: Site of three decisive battles, with a museum telling their story and the tomb of Ibrahim Lodi.

destinations.name: Surajkund
destinations.blurb: Famous for its international crafts fair each February, held beside a 10th-century reservoir.

destinations.name: Rakhigarhi
destinations.blurb: One of the largest Harappan sites in India, with ongoing excavations and a small museum.

destinations.name: Kalesar National Park
destinations.blurb: Sal forest in the Shivalik foothills along the Yamuna, with leopards, elephants and quiet forest rest houses.

devotional.name: Brahma Sarovar, Kurukshetra
devotional.blurb: A vast sacred tank where lakhs of Hindus bathe during solar eclipses, set at the heart of the Mahabharata landscape.

devotional.name: Jyotisar
devotional.blurb: The banyan tree near Kurukshetra where Krishna is believed to have recited the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna.

devotional.name: Pehowa
devotional.blurb: An ancient tirtha on the Saraswati where families perform rites for ancestors and keep genealogies with local priests.

devotional.name: Mata Mansa Devi Temple
devotional.blurb: A Shakti shrine in Panchkula near Chandigarh, crowded during the Navratri melas.

devotional.name: Gurdwara Panjokhra Sahib
devotional.blurb: A gurdwara near Ambala marking the stay of Guru Har Krishan on his way to Delhi.

devotional.name: Dargah of Bu Ali Shah Qalandar
devotional.blurb: The 14th-century tomb of a revered Sufi saint in Panipat, where visitors tie threads and offer prayers on Thursdays.

devotional.name: Adi Badri
devotional.blurb: A wooded site in Yamunanagar held to be the source of the Saraswati, with Hindu temples and the remains of a Buddhist stupa.

highlights: Evening aarti at Brahma Sarovar in Kurukshetra
Winter birdwatching at Sultanpur
Walk the terraces of Pinjore Gardens
Lakeside picnic in the Morni Hills
Shop for crafts at the Surajkund Mela in February
See Harappan mounds at Rakhigarhi

days.title: Sultanpur birding
days.details: Arrive in Delhi or Gurugram and drive about 1 hour to Sultanpur National Park for an afternoon of birdwatching.

days.title: Panipat to Kurukshetra
days.details: Drive about 2.5 hours to Panipat for the battle museum, then 1 hour on to Kurukshetra for the evening aarti at Brahma Sarovar.

days.title: Kurukshetra
days.details: Visit Jyotisar, the Krishna Museum, the Kurukshetra Panorama and Sannihit Sarovar.

days.title: Pinjore and departure
days.details: Drive about 2 hours to Pinjore Gardens, then on to Chandigarh airport or station.

days.title: Arrive Gurugram
days.details: Settle in and spend the late afternoon birding at Sultanpur National Park.

days.title: Gurugram to Hisar via Rakhigarhi
days.details: Drive about 3 hours to the Harappan site of Rakhigarhi, then 1 hour on to Hisar.

days.title: Hisar to Kurukshetra
days.details: Visit the Firoz Shah palace complex in Hisar, then drive about 3 hours to Kurukshetra.

days.title: Kurukshetra
days.details: A full day at Brahma Sarovar, Jyotisar, the Krishna Museum and the Panorama, ending with the evening aarti.

days.title: Pinjore and Morni Hills
days.details: Drive about 2 hours to Pinjore Gardens, then climb 1 hour to Morni Hills for a lakeside evening.

days.title: Departure
days.details: Drive about 1 hour down to Chandigarh for your onward flight or train.

name: Himachal Pradesh
tagline: Apple orchards, cedar forests and the high desert of Spiti
intro: Himachal Pradesh rises from the colonial hill towns of Shimla and Dalhousie to the cold desert valleys of Spiti and Lahaul. Manali and the Kullu valley are classic family trips, McLeod Ganj is the home of the Tibetan government in exile, and Bir draws paragliders from around the world. Spiti and Chandratal are summer-only, when the high passes are open.
bestTime: March to June and September to November
photoAlt: Key Monastery stacked on a conical hill above the Spiti River valley

destinations.name: Shimla
destinations.blurb: The old summer capital of British India, with the Mall Road, Christ Church and the toy train from Kalka.

destinations.name: Manali
destinations.blurb: A base for Solang Valley, the Atal Tunnel and the old wooden houses and cafes of Old Manali.

destinations.name: Dharamshala and McLeod Ganj
destinations.blurb: The home of the Tibetan government-in-exile, with cafes, the Tibet Museum and the day trek to Triund.

destinations.name: Spiti Valley
destinations.blurb: A high-altitude cold desert of fossil villages, the Chandratal lake and some of the starriest skies in India.

destinations.name: Kinnaur
destinations.blurb: Apple country along the Sutlej, with the villages of Sangla, Chitkul and Kalpa facing the Kinner Kailash range.

destinations.name: Bir Billing
destinations.blurb: One of the world's top paragliding sites, with Tibetan colonies and tea gardens below.

destinations.name: Dalhousie and Khajjiar
destinations.blurb: Quiet colonial hill towns and a meadow ringed by deodar forest in the Chamba district.

destinations.name: Kasol and the Parvati Valley
destinations.blurb: A riverside village under pine forest, with trails to Kheerganga's hot pool and the village of Tosh.

devotional.name: Tsuglagkhang, McLeod Ganj
devotional.blurb: The Dalai Lama's temple complex, where Tibetans walk the kora path and gather for his public teachings.

devotional.name: Hadimba Devi Temple
devotional.blurb: A 16th-century wooden pagoda temple in a cedar forest in Manali, built around a rock where the goddess Hadimba is said to have meditated.

devotional.name: Key Monastery
devotional.blurb: A Gelugpa monastery stacked on a hill above the Spiti river, home to monks and a collection of old thangkas.

devotional.name: Tabo Monastery
devotional.blurb: Founded in 996 CE, this mud-walled monastery in Spiti holds some of the finest early Buddhist murals in the Himalaya.

devotional.name: Gurdwara Manikaran Sahib
devotional.blurb: A gurdwara in the Parvati Valley beside boiling hot springs, where the langar rice is cooked in the natural heat.

devotional.name: Jwalamukhi Temple
devotional.blurb: A Shakti Peetha in Kangra where natural gas flames burn from the rock and are worshipped as the goddess.

devotional.name: Naina Devi Temple
devotional.blurb: A hilltop Shakti Peetha above Gobind Sagar in Bilaspur district, busy during Navratri and the Shravan fair.

devotional.name: Baijnath Temple
devotional.blurb: A 13th-century stone Shiva temple in the Kangra valley, with the Dhauladhar range as its backdrop.

highlights: Ride the Kalka–Shimla toy train
Drive through the Atal Tunnel to Sissu in Lahaul
Tandem paragliding at Bir Billing
Visit Key Monastery and the high village of Kibber
Camp beside Chandratal Lake in summer
Attend prayers at the Tsuglagkhang in McLeod Ganj

days.title: Chandigarh to Shimla
days.details: Drive about 3.5 hours up to Shimla, or ride the toy train from Kalka. Evening stroll along the Mall Road and the Ridge.

days.title: Shimla and Kufri
days.details: Visit Jakhu Temple, the Viceregal Lodge and Kufri, about 45 minutes away.

days.title: Shimla to Manali
days.details: A full-day drive of about 8 hours via Mandi and the Kullu valley, with a stop for river views at Pandoh Dam.

days.title: Solang and the Atal Tunnel
days.details: Drive through the Atal Tunnel to Sissu in Lahaul, then stop at Solang Valley on the way back. Evening in Old Manali.

days.title: Manali and departure
days.details: Visit Hadimba Temple and the Vashisht hot springs, then transfer to Bhuntar airport, about 1.5 hours away.

itineraries.title: Kinnaur and Spiti Circuit (June to September)

days.title: Arrive Shimla
days.details: Drive from Chandigarh to Shimla, about 3.5 hours, and rest for the journey ahead.

days.title: Shimla to Sangla
days.details: Follow the Sutlej through Narkanda and Rampur to the Baspa valley, about 7–8 hours.

days.title: Chitkul and Kalpa
days.details: Morning visit to Chitkul, the last village before Tibet, then drive about 2.5 hours to Kalpa for views of the Kinner Kailash.

days.title: Kalpa to Tabo via Nako
days.details: Drive about 6 hours along the Sutlej and into Spiti, stopping at Nako Lake. Evening at the 10th-century Tabo Monastery.

days.title: Tabo to Kaza via Dhankar
days.details: Visit the cliffside Dhankar Monastery and the Pin Valley turn-off, then drive on to Kaza, about 2 hours in total.

days.title: Key, Kibber, Langza and Hikkim
days.details: A day around Kaza visiting Key Monastery, the high village of Kibber, Langza's fossil beds and the post office at Hikkim.

days.title: Kaza to Chandratal
days.details: Cross Kunzum Pass, about 4 hours, to camp near Chandratal Lake. Walk to the lake for the evening light.

days.title: Chandratal to Manali
days.details: Drive via Batal and Gramphu, then through the Atal Tunnel to Manali, about 5–6 hours.

days.title: Departure
days.details: Transfer to Bhuntar airport, about 1.5 hours away, or take an overnight bus to Delhi.

name: Jharkhand
tagline: Plateau waterfalls, sal forests and sunrise at Netarhat
intro: Jharkhand sits on the Chota Nagpur plateau, where rivers tumble off its edges in a string of waterfalls around Ranchi. Further west, Netarhat's viewpoints and the elephant forests of Betla offer quiet nature trips, while Deoghar and Parasnath draw large numbers of pilgrims. Ranchi is well connected by air.
photoAlt: Hundru Falls dropping over rocky ledges of the Subarnarekha River near Ranchi

destinations.name: Ranchi
destinations.blurb: The capital and a base for several waterfalls, with Tagore Hill, Rock Garden and Kanke Dam in town.

destinations.name: Hundru Falls
destinations.blurb: The Subarnarekha River drops nearly 100 metres here, about 45 km from Ranchi.

destinations.name: Netarhat
destinations.blurb: A plateau hill station known for its sunrise and sunset points over forested valleys.

destinations.name: Betla National Park
destinations.blurb: Part of the Palamau Tiger Reserve, with elephants, gaur and the ruins of two Chero forts.

destinations.name: Patratu Valley
destinations.blurb: A winding ghat road above the Patratu dam, popular for its hairpin bends and lake views.

destinations.name: Jamshedpur
destinations.blurb: India's first planned industrial city, with Jubilee Park and the Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary nearby.

destinations.name: Dassam Falls
destinations.blurb: The Kanchi River drops about 44 metres over a rocky ledge south-east of Ranchi, fullest in the months after the monsoon.

devotional.name: Baidyanath Dham, Deoghar
devotional.blurb: A Jyotirlinga temple where pilgrims carry Ganga water about 105 km on foot from Sultanganj during the Shravani Mela.

devotional.name: Shikharji
devotional.blurb: The summit temples of Parasnath Hill, where 20 of the 24 Jain Tirthankaras attained moksha, reached by a 27 km round-trip walk.

devotional.name: Rajrappa
devotional.blurb: The Chhinnamasta Temple stands where the Bhairavi river meets the Damodar, a major Tantric shrine that draws crowds at Navratri.

devotional.name: Jagannath Temple, Ranchi
devotional.blurb: A 1691 hilltop temple modelled on Puri's, which holds its own Rath Yatra each summer.

devotional.name: Basukinath
devotional.blurb: A Shiva temple in Dumka district that many pilgrims visit right after Deoghar to complete their journey.

devotional.name: Itkhori
devotional.blurb: A site in Chatra district sacred to Hindus, Buddhists and Jains, with the Bhadrakali temple and old carved stupas.

highlights: See Hundru, Dassam and Jonha falls in a day from Ranchi
Sunset at Magnolia Point in Netarhat
Jeep safari in Betla National Park
Drive the hairpin bends of Patratu Valley
Visit the Chhinnamasta Temple at Rajrappa
Climb Parasnath Hill to the Shikharji shrines

days.title: Arrive Ranchi
days.details: Visit Tagore Hill and the Jagannath Temple, with an evening at Kanke Dam.

days.title: Hundru and Jonha falls
days.details: Drive about 1.5 hours to Hundru Falls and walk down to the pool, then visit nearby Jonha Falls on the way back.

days.title: Dassam Falls and Rajrappa
days.details: Visit Dassam Falls, about 1 hour from Ranchi, then drive to the Chhinnamasta Temple at Rajrappa at the meeting of the Damodar and Bhairavi rivers.

days.title: Patratu Valley and departure
days.details: Morning drive through the Patratu Valley bends, about 1 hour away, then transfer to Ranchi airport.

days.title: Arrive Ranchi
days.details: Settle in and visit Tagore Hill and the Jagannath Temple.

days.title: Ranchi waterfalls
days.details: A day trip to Hundru, Jonha and Dassam falls, returning to Ranchi for the night.

days.title: Ranchi to Netarhat
days.details: Drive about 4 hours west through Gumla to Netarhat, arriving in time for sunset at Magnolia Point.

days.title: Netarhat to Betla via Lodh Falls
days.details: Catch sunrise at Netarhat, visit Lodh Falls, the highest waterfall in the state, then drive on to Betla, about 4 hours in total.

days.title: Betla National Park
days.details: Morning jeep safari for elephants and gaur, then explore the old and new Palamu forts in the afternoon.

days.title: Betla to Ranchi via Patratu
days.details: Drive about 4.5 hours back toward Ranchi, with a detour along the Patratu Valley road.

days.title: Departure
days.details: Transfer to Ranchi airport for your onward flight.
